provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Grants a claim already on the table as true and then treats it as making no difference: いくら安いとしたって三つは多すぎる. The sibling lane instead supposes something that has not come about (明日から始めるとしたって). With a noun it grants one party as a case in point (会社としたって、そんな余裕はない). Colloquial for としても; polite としましても.

examples.ruby: いくら安[やす]いとしたって、三[みっ]つも買[か]うのは多[おお]すぎる。
examples.english: Even granting they're cheap, buying three of them is too many.

examples.ruby: 先輩[せんぱい]の言[い]い分[ぶん]が正[ただ]しいとしたって、今[いま]さら計画[けいかく]は変[か]えられない。
examples.english: Even granting my senior's version of it is right, the plan can't be changed at this point.

examples.ruby: 冗談[じょうだん]だとしたって、その言[い]い方[かた]はひどすぎる。
examples.english: Even granting it was a joke, that's a terrible way to put it.

patterns.usage_note: Grants a case that actually exists — a person, a place, an organization — as an extreme or representative example, with a deflating or negative clause after it (部長にしたってこの状況は予想外だった). Sibling lanes suppose a case that has not come about (手伝うにしたって), add a further party the same thing holds of (親にしたって), or sweep in every case after an interrogative (誰にしたって). にしたところで adds that it would make no difference.

examples.ruby: 部長[ぶちょう]にしたって、この状況[じょうきょう]は予想外[よそうがい]だっただろう。
examples.english: Even the boss can't have seen this situation coming.

examples.ruby: この駅[えき]にしたって、昔[むかし]は畑[はたけ]しかなかったそうだ。
examples.english: Even this station — there was nothing but fields here once, they say.

examples.ruby: あの大[おお]きな会社[かいしゃ]にしたって、始[はじ]めは社員[しゃいん]が三人[さんにん]だけだったんだ。
examples.english: Even that big company had only three employees when it started.

glosses: even if you had … , it would have made no difference
no matter how much you had …
patterns.usage_note: Looks back on a settled past and denies that a different action would have changed it: the outcome is already known and the effort would have been futile anyway (あのとき走ったところで間に合わなかっただろう). The 仮定 sibling supposes an action still open now and denies it in the non-past (今から急いだところで間に合わない). What precedes it is counterfactual, not something actually done; for an effort really made, のに or ても is used.

examples.ruby: あのとき謝[あやま]ったところで、彼女[かのじょ]の気持[きも]ちは変[か]わらなかっただろう。
examples.english: Even if I had apologized back then, it wouldn't have changed how she felt.

examples.ruby: あのとき頼[たの]んだとこで、彼[かれ]は来[き]てくれなかったと思[おも]う。
examples.english: Even if I'd asked him then, I don't think he would have come.

examples.ruby: どんなに急[いそ]いだところで、あの日[ひ]の飛行機[ひこうき]には乗[の]れなかったはずだ。
examples.english: No matter how much I'd hurried, there's no way I would have made that day's flight.

patterns.usage_note: Grants something already established (忙しかったにしろ, 短い付き合いにしろ) and insists the main point stands regardless. Sibling entries concede a supposition that has not come about (値上げするにしろ) or raise a noun as a case that is no exception (新人にしろ). Nouns and な-adjectives take である before it in careful writing, and the form sits between the written にせよ and the conversational にしても.

examples.ruby: 本人[ほんにん]が忙[いそが]しかったにしろ、返事[へんじ]くらいはできたはずだ。
examples.english: Granted he was busy, he could at least have answered.

examples.ruby: 短[みじか]い付[つ]き合[あ]いにしろ、隣[となり]の店主[てんしゅ]の人柄[ひとがら]はよく分[わ]かった。
examples.english: Short as our acquaintance was, I got a clear sense of what the shopkeeper next door was like.

examples.ruby: 以前[いぜん]断[ことわ]られたにしろ、頼[たの]み直[なお]す価値[かち]はあると思[おも]う。
examples.english: Granted they turned us down before, I still think it's worth asking again.
